mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Thursday, September 17, 2026. Baseten, an AI inference provider, has launched a new safety partnership through its research arm, Base Labs, in collaboration with Hugging Face and Goodfire AI. The initiative aims to develop a standard for safety evaluation and monitoring specifically for open-weight models. These models face increasing scrutiny due to a technique called abliteration, which allows users to remove safety safeguards; Hugging Face currently hosts over 6,000 such models. The partners intend to move away from "bolted-on" safety features, instead advocating for transparency and controls built directly into the model training and deployment process. Goodfire AI, which focuses on model interpretability, is expected to provide the technical expertise for opening the "black box" of AI decision-making. By creating an open, collaborative standard, the partners hope to provide a transparent alternative to closed-source development, arguing that public visibility is an advantage for safety. This initiative arrives as Baseten and Goodfire, both well-capitalized firms, seek to rally the broader developer ecosystem to contribute to this framework. OpenAI has introduced a new framework for disclosing instances of model misalignment, defined as unexpected or concerning model behavior. Previously, the company’s reporting was ad hoc, often consolidated into system cards for new releases. Under the new framework, OpenAI plans to publish findings more frequently, even when the behavior is not yet fully explained or mitigated. The company states that as frontier models advance, the industry lacks explicit standards for disclosing these issues. OpenAI intends for this framework to provide evidence that can be examined by external researchers and policymakers, prioritizing findings that challenge existing safety assumptions. This proactive disclosure model is designed to facilitate a better-informed consensus on AI progress, helping other developers identify potential pitfalls as their own systems scale. Pinterest is expanding its AI capabilities with a new consumer-facing feature called Restyle. Currently in beta for users in the United States and Canada, the tool allows individuals to upload photos of their rooms and use prompts to digitally rearrange decor, swap furniture, or change lighting and paint colors. Powered by Pinterest Intelligence—which leverages Nvidia Blackwell graphics processing units—the feature is designed to connect inspiration from saved pins directly to potential purchases. By allowing users to visualize products in their own living spaces, Pinterest aims to reduce the friction between discovery and acquisition. The company intends to roll the tool out more broadly next month, signaling a shift toward using generative AI to convert passive inspiration into concrete shopping behavior. In infrastructure news, Amazon Web Services has provided guidance on selecting vector store backends for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. Retrieval Augmented Generation architectures rely on vector databases to translate text into mathematical vectors, allowing large language models to perform semantic searches and generate more relevant responses. AWS highlights three supported options for customer-managed configurations: Amazon OpenSearch Service for high-speed performance, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector for relational database integration, and Amazon S3 Vectors, which AWS claims can reduce storage costs by up to 90 percent. Choosing the appropriate backend is critical for performance and cost management, as these databases serve as the bridge between raw data and the contextual understanding required by AI agents. Separately, AWS introduced an automated, serverless pipeline for collecting Git metrics, intended to help engineering teams measure the impact of AI coding tools on developer velocity. By establishing a baseline and tracking metrics over time, teams can empirically verify if AI tools are truly increasing productivity or merely introducing unexpected quality issues. Also in the industry, the International Meteor Organization, which tracks meteor phenomena, reported that it has suffered a critical cyberattack. The nonprofit stated that the attack damaged aging infrastructure, forcing much of its website offline for several weeks.
